definition: OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision Library) is a library of programming functions mainly for real-time computer vision.
details: Originally developed by Intel, it was later supported by Willow Garage, then Itseez (which was later acquired by Intel). The library is cross-platform and licensed as free and open-source software under Apache License 2. Starting in 2011, OpenCV features GPU acceleration for real-time operations.

explainer.lead: How to install OpenCV, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Started at Intel Research in 1999 (Gary Bradski); now maintained by the non-profit OpenCV.org.

install.javascript: npm install @techstark/opencv-js   # community build of opencv.js

quickstart.python:
import cv2

img = cv2.imread("photo.jpg")
gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
edges = cv2.Canny(gray, 100, 200)
small = cv2.resize(img, (224, 224))       # model-ready size
cv2.imwrite("edges.png", edges)
